general_notice: This is general preparedness information. It is not a location-specific instruction, evacuation order, or statement that any place is safe. Follow instructions issued by NDMA, the relevant PDMA / GBDMA / SDMA, district administration and local authorities.

sources.name: Know Before You Go — avalanche awareness programme
WMO / national meteorological services — snowfall and weather advisories (Pakistan Meteorological Department)

audiences.title: Communities in avalanche-prone valleys
items: Know which slopes and gullies above your village have produced avalanches before; local memory is valuable evidence.
Heavy snowfall over 1–3 days, strong wind and rapid warming are the main warning signs; avoid open slopes and gully floors during and after such periods.
Agree family meeting points and a communication plan before the winter season.
Keep a winter kit: warm clothing, torch, radio, first-aid supplies, essential medicines and food for several days.
Report snow cracking, recent slides or 'whumpf' sounds to local authorities.

audiences.title: Travellers and tourists
items: Check official weather advisories and road status from authorities before travelling into mountain districts.
Do not stop under steep snow-loaded slopes or in avalanche runout zones; pass through quickly, one vehicle at a time where authorities advise.
Carry warm clothing, water, food and a charged phone; tell someone your route and expected arrival.
Follow closures and instructions from police, district administration and road authorities.

audiences.title: Road operators (NHA, FWO, PWD)
items: Maintain a register of known avalanche paths crossing roads, with chainage and historical activity.
Pre-position snow-clearing equipment and crews at either side of known avalanche corridors.
Coordinate any closure decisions with district administration and communicate them through official channels only.

audiences.title: Response teams (Rescue 1122, district teams, PDMAs)
items: Survival chances fall sharply after the first 15–30 minutes of burial; organised immediate companion rescue matters most.
Equip teams with transceivers, probes and shovels, and train in their use before the season.
Assess secondary avalanche risk before committing rescuers to a debris field.
